answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with portable, decaying reputation: each identity earns trust only by completing attested work over time, and that score decays without fresh contributions, like snow melting off a tundra knoll each spring. A new identity starts on a bare ledge with zero standing and must climb slowly, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents faces a steep time-and-work cost per identity instead of a free copy. Forged histories are exposed because peers cross-check attested work receipts before trusting a newcomer.
